answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the knoll check immediately, the anchor audit keeps the resolved set and the orchard replay reveals exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 200 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 200 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
